title: Why it matters that President Trump just dialed into a NASA news conference
author: Eric Berger
body: As is standard procedure for major NASA missions, the US space agency held a post-launch news conference on Sunday morning at Kennedy Space Center in Florida to provide information about how the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope was faring during its initial maneuvers. What was not standard, however, is what happened in the middle of the news conference. A little less than half an hour in, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman looked down at his mobile phone, and then stood up and walked away from the dais where he had been seated behind a table along with other NASA officials. He briefly left the room. Isaacman returned about a minute later, phone in hand, apologizing for interrupting NASA's chief of science, Nicky Fox, as she was speaking about the mission. title: Google changes Lake Ontario to Lake America in Search, Google Maps
body: Are you visiting the Great Lakes before the end of summer? You may notice something odd when planning out the trip on Google. Lake Ontario is no more. Google Maps has renamed it to "Lake America." Lake America on Google Maps Credit: Google Maps Try typing "Lake Ontario" into Google Search as well. Google takes users to a search results page for "Lake America." Lake America on Google Search Credit: Google Search Last week, amid an ongoing trade war with Canada, President Donald Trump issued an executive order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America. "In recognition of this flourishing economic resource and its critical importance to our Nation s economy and its people, I am directing that the Lake officially be renamed as Lake America," Trump said in his order, while taking a few swipes at Canada. Google, likely anticipating that the change would be divisive, issued a statement on its News from Google website. "The U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) has formally changed the name for 'Lake Ontario' to 'Lake America' in the United States," the company said. "Since we update Google Maps to reflect name changes in official government sources, which is GNIS for the U.S., people using Maps in the U.S. will see 'Lake America,' those in Canada will continue to see 'Lake Ontario,' and those outside of the U.S. and Canada will see both names. These updates follow our long-standing policy for bodies of water with names that vary from country to country, and are starting to roll out now." title: NASAs Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launches in historic moment
body: NASA 's latest flagship telescope is on its way to a million‑mile‑distant orbit to map the universe and hunt for distant planets. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope lifted off at 7:26 a.m. ET on Sunday from Cape Canaveral, Florida. Riding a SpaceX Falcon Heavy, the spacecraft separated from its rocket and began its space journey. Mission leaders say Roman will reshape astronomy by pairing a wide, sharp view of the universe with powerful tools to probe dark matter , dark energy, and distant exoplanets . Play our Big Guessing Game: Make your predictions now for a chance to win a new Apple Watch. Time's running out! The observatory, with a lifecycle cost of about $4.3 billion, will make its data public as soon as it's processed. And what a firehose of data it's expected to collect. Hubble gathered 172 terabytes of science data in its first 30 years; Roman will downlink about 1.4 terabytes every day , said Nicky Fox, associate administrator for science at NASA. What Roman can do in a single month to survey the Milky Way would take Hubble about 100 years . "The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is a sheer powerhouse," Fox said. "It is literally a speed machine. The speed at which we'll be scanning the sky, delivering vast amounts of data, and returning results will be at an unprecedented rate never done before." title: Inside Meta’s push to put robots to work in data centers
author: Paresh Dave, WIRED.com
body: Meta is testing robots that can plug in cables, reset servers, and handle other tasks inside its data centers , according to several current and former workers familiar with the projects. The ongoing effort, which has not been previously reported, may eventually allow Meta to operate its rapidly expanding data center footprint with fewer humans, keeping labor costs in check as its spending on AI infrastructure soars . Meta is using robots and related hardware from several different vendors, including Watney Robotics, Kinova, and ABB, according to the same workers, who asked to remain anonymous because they weren’t authorized to speak to the media. Kinova and ABB declined to comment. Watney didn’t respond to requests for comment. In one experiment, Meta is evaluating whether a Kinova Gen3 robotic arm could be used for power cycling or cutting off electricity to servers. The company is also testing a different robot to swap networking cables. One Meta data center worker estimates that if it’s successful, the bot could replace up to 80 percent of some people’s workloads. “We thought those of us performing the physical tasks were safe for a while, but not anymore,” says the worker. “It’s coming for us all, unfortunately.” Read full article Comments

NASA and SpaceX are targeting the launch of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope no earlier than 7:26 a.m. ET on Aug. 30 at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida. The infrared telescope's ride, a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket, will lift off from the historic Launch Complex 39A pad, the same that sent Apollo 11 and the maiden voyage of the Space Shuttle into orbit. Roman, with a lifecycle cost of about $4.3 billion, combines Hubble-like sharpness with a field of view at least 100 times larger, allowing scientists to map billions of galaxies, probe dark energy and dark matter , and discover exoplanets at an unprecedented scale. The telescope sees the universe in infrared light, which human eyes cannot see. Its wide surveys let astronomers track how structures, such as stars, galaxies, and galaxy clusters, grow over time, as well as measure how the universe expands. Mission planners expect Roman images from a major survey to include more than 2 billion galaxies and, over time, reveal tens of thousands of supernova explosions and many new planets. Tonight with just your naked eye, you'll be able to see the Mare Serenitatis, the Copernicus Crater, and the Oceanus Procellarum. If you do have viewing equipment, such as binoculars, you'll also see the Mare Frigoris, the Archimedes Crater, and the Apennine Mountains. If you have access to a telescope, you'll also be able to see the Apollo 15 and 16 landing spots, and the Rima Ariadaeus. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on September 26. What are Moon phases? The Moon's appearance changes throughout the month as it moves through its different phases. It takes roughly 29.5 days for the Moon to complete one full cycle as it orbits Earth, according to NASA . The phase we see depends on the Moon's position relative to the Sun and Earth, which determines how much of its sunlit side is visible to us. Over the course of the cycle, the Moon changes from a slim crescent to a half Moon and eventually a Full Moon, before beginning the process again. title: Robert De Niro & Adam Scott on How The Whisper Man Tackles Generational Trauma
body: In advance of the release of Netflix's new thriller The Whisper Man , Mashable executive producer Mark Stetson sat down with stars Robert De Niro, Adam Scott, director James Ashcroft, and author Alex North to discuss the film's theme of generational trauma, the complex dynamics between fathers and sons, and the process of adapting the highly anticipated novel for the screen. Author of the book, Alex North discussed the book's themes that were most important to translate to film: "This is a book that I wanted to write because it was about fathers and sons, and grandfathers and fathers and sons. And different iterations of the way that plays out in terms of generational trauma. How we respond to things that have happened in our childhood, how we protect our children from things that have happened in our childhood, how we pass things down and how we don't." Adam Scott was particularly drawn to North's themes. "I thought it was a really interesting part of the script, this horrifying trauma that they are both going through while simultaneously trying to repair their relationship." De Niro added, "It was one of the things that attracted me to the script, that relationship." At the close of the interview, Robert De Niro shares his candid advice for young actors who experience imposter syndrome when working with their heroes: "If it manifests in a such a way where it gets in the way of working on a scene, I'd say, 'It's ok, don't worry. In two days, it's all going to go away. It's just us." The Whisper Man is now streaming on Netflix.

title: I asked 100 companies for my data. Some deleted it instead.
author: Reece Rodgers, wired.com
body: I filed a request with McDonald’s earlier this month to access all of the personal data the fast food company collected about me, and I received a stunning 515-page report a few days later that detailed my app interactions in granular detail and predicted I would never stop eating there. Under the California Consumer Privacy Act , I have the legal right to request access to information from large companies that collect personal data. So I was curious what others might have on me, and I spent the next week filing more than 100 requests. The CCPA went into effect in 2020, and three of its key provisions are the right to opt out of the selling of personal information, the right to delete that info, and the right to request a copy for yourself. title: Adults Season 2s most foul-mouthed scene is also its biggest romantic gesture
body: In most rom-coms, a romantic gesture looks like running through an airport to make one last declaration of love, or writing a yearning letter every day for a year. In Adults , it looks like saying "cunt" on every man-on-the-street interview show you can find. SEE ALSO: 'Adults' assembles the Avengers of man-on-the-street creators The gesture in question comes in Season 2, episode 7, titled "C Alert." In the episode, Anton (Owen Thiele) mistakenly talks to his co-workers the way he talks to his friends, saying "cunt alert!" in a company meeting. He doesn't mean it as an insult, drawing instead on its positive meaning rooted in the queer ballroom scene. That meaning has led to a wider resurgence of the term, including in online spaces , but it's still viewed as unforgivably rude in some places, including Anton's office, which skews older, and likely less queer. In an effort to help save Anton's job, his housemate and yearning love interest Paul Baker ( Jack Innanen ) decides to try normalizing saying "cunt" in the workplace by dropping it into as many viral interview shows as he can. It's a moment Adults co-creator Ben Kronengold describes as an "ugly sweet" step in Anton and Paul Baker's romance. While the pair obviously care about one another, any attempts to be together have stalled due to a house-wide rule forbidding dating within the friend group. title: Paranormal Activity is a bad omen for Broadway
body: Nowadays on Broadway , you've got to have a gimmick. It's not enough to be beloved or even acclaimed. Just look at Cats: The Jellicle Ball, a bodacious revival that re-imagined Andrew Lloyd Webber's Broadway smash as a ballroom runway, bringing the audience into the experience and onto the stage. Critics cheered, audiences clacked their fans in appreciation, and the Tonys gave three awards, including Best Direction of a Musical. Yet, none of that stopped The Jellicle Ball from closing weeks after it received those Tony flowers. Even a grateful community that loved Cats, Webber, or ballroom culture couldn't keep Jellicle Ball rolling. So, it's little surprise that Broadway producers are favoring a seemingly endless array of theatrical adaptations of movies, TV, and other popular IP. Just this year, Broadway saw The Lost Boys: A New Musical , Titanique , Schmigadoon , and Dog Day Afternoon competing for crowds, while Heated Rivalry got an off-Broadway unofficial parody faster than it got a vinyl soundtrack release . Some of these were marvelous, others interesting, and then there was Beaches . title: Adults assembles the Avengers of man-on-the-street creators
body: If you use social media , you've seen a man-on-the-street interview. You know the type: punchy, short-form digital series where you get to know an interviewee in record time. Some shows, such as Track Star or Gaydar , use specific subjects like music or queer history as entry points. Others, like Are You Okay? or Subway Takes , invite guests to rant about a topic of their choosing. These series have taken over your feeds and Hollywood press tours alike, and for one episode, they take over FX's sitcom Adults . SEE ALSO: 'Adults' Season 2 is the hardest I've laughed at a sitcom this year In Adults Season 2, episode 7, titled "C Alert," Paul Baker ( Jack Innanen ) laments having what he and his friends call "man-on-the-street face," a condition that makes him a target for New York City's street interview content creators . (Due to his Canadian politeness, he can never turn them down.) However, by the episode's end, Paul Baker embraces his man-on-the-street face to help his housemate/will-they-won't-they love interest Anton (Owen Thiele), who's gotten in trouble at work for saying "cunt." While the word's positive connotations in queer ballroom culture have led to wider reclamation and resurgence, especially online , it still carries quite a bit of baggage in America; hence Paul Baker's quest to encourage its normalization through street interviews. title: AEW All In 2026: The non-fans guide to the massive wrestling event.
body: While not as established as its contemporary, All Elite Wrestling, or AEW, is perhaps the best showcase of professional wrestling in the United States and the wider world. It's why AEW is "Where the best wrestle." For that simple reason, it's a no-brainer that AEW's biggest event of the year, All In , is must-watch TV. The fourth annual event is the culmination of years and years worth of television on the company's weekly shows, AEW Dynamite and Collison and the showcase of the company's future pillars. The big issue, though, is that unlike the WWE, which has decades of insular storytelling to rely on, making it easy for fans to follow rivalries and feuds, AEW does not have that. In fact, its roster comprises wrestlers with decades of experience and ties elsewhere in the independent scene, to the point that these ties bleed into the storylines told in AEW. That makes it hard to get into some storylines, because, if you weren't watching CHIKARA in the late 2010s, you'd have no idea why Eddie Kingston really, really hates Claudio Castagnoli (fka Cesaro in WWE). For the most part, as the company is now 7 years old, that problem is mostly faded away, but for those who don't watch pro wrestling as much or are used to the mainstays and tropes of WWE, getting to know and care about AEW's cast of athletes and genetic freaks can be a challenge. That's what this guide is for. What are Moon phases? The Moon's appearance changes throughout the month as it moves through its different phases. It takes roughly 29.5 days for the Moon to complete one full cycle as it orbits Earth, according to NASA . title: NYT Pips hints, answers for August 29, 2026
body: Welcome to your guide to Pips, the latest game in the New York Times catalog. Released in August 2025, Pips puts a unique spin on dominoes, creating a fun single-player experience that could become your next daily gaming habit. Currently, if you're stuck, the game only offers to reveal the entire puzzle, forcing you to move on to the next difficulty level and start over. However, we have you covered! Below are piecemeal answers that will serve as hints so that you can find your way through each difficulty level. How to play Pips If you've ever played dominoes, you'll have a passing familiarity with how Pips is played. As we've shared in our previous hints stories for Pips, the tiles, like dominoes, are placed vertically or horizontally and connect with each other. The main difference between a traditional game of dominoes and Pips is the color-coded conditions you have to address. The touching tiles don't necessarily have to match. title: Court ruling deals Kashi major setback
body: Nevada can ban the prediction market platform Kalshi from operating in the state, the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled Friday. In March 2025 , the Nevada Gaming Control Board sent a cease-and-desist letter to Kalshi, arguing that the company operated a sports betting platform in the state, in violation of Nevada gaming regulations. Kalshi disagreed, characterizing itself as a "designated contract market" (DCM) that offers legal sports event contracts, or "swaps." Nonetheless, its own marketing copy advertised Kalshi as "the first app for legal sports betting in all 50 states," according to the ruling . SEE ALSO: New York sues Kalshi, claiming it's 'unlicensed gambling' "The substance of the sports event contracts offered on Kalshi s DCM is sports gambling, regardless of whether Kalshi calls them swaps," Judge Ryan D. Nelson wrote in the opinion. The judges' unanimous 3-0 decision spells trouble for Kalshi and other prediction market companies that allow people to effectively gamble on sports. "This completely vindicates what we have been saying all along," Mike Dreitzer, Nevada Gaming Control Board Chairman, said in a statement . "This is sports betting and needs to be properly regulated by the state." Kalshi spokeswoman Dani Lever said the company will seek further review, according to the Nevada Independent . At the heart of the matter is whether, as Kalshi argued, the Commodity Exchange Act, a federal law that regulates the trading of commodity futures, preempts state gaming regulations as they apply to swaps. title: Heres how to watch NASAs Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launch live
body: If the weather plays nice, NASA plans to launch its next flagship space observatory this Sunday, and viewers can watch the coverage live online from home. NASA and SpaceX are targeting the launch of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope no earlier than 7:26 a.m. ET on Aug. 30 at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida. The infrared telescope's ride, a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket, will lift off from the historic Launch Complex 39A pad, the same that sent Apollo 11 and the maiden voyage of the Space Shuttle into orbit. Play our Big Guessing Game: Make your predictions now for a chance to win a new Apple Watch. Time's running out! Roman, with a lifecycle cost of about $4.3 billion, combines Hubble-like sharpness with a field of view at least 100 times larger, allowing scientists to map billions of galaxies, probe dark energy and dark matter , and discover exoplanets at an unprecedented scale. The telescope sees the universe in infrared light, which human eyes cannot see. Its wide surveys let astronomers track how structures, such as stars, galaxies, and galaxy clusters, grow over time, as well as measure how the universe expands. Mission planners expect Roman images from a major survey to include more than 2 billion galaxies and, over time, reveal tens of thousands of supernova explosions and many new planets. title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says AGI is already here — and the milestone is senseless
body: Some AI industry leaders, such as OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, are obsessed with artificial general intelligence , or AGI. While the term has no universally agreed-upon definition, it generally refers to AI that can match or even surpass human cognitive abilities across a large range of tasks. In a recent interview , Altman shared that OpenAI believes it will achieve AGI by the end of the year. However, according to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, AI has, in some respects, already achieved AGI and it's really no big deal. Nvidia has become the darling of the tech industry in recent years. The company is an invaluable part of the AI industry because it produces many of the high-performance chips that power the technology. During an earnings call on Aug. 26, Huang was asked about AGI in light of OpenAI's recent claims. "For many tasks, we could say that we ve already achieved AGI," Huang said. "I think of all of those milestones they re kind of senseless at this point." Huang said the focus should be on whether AI is "doing productive and useful work." From a company perspective, Huang added that the concern should be about "generating profitable tokens." It's unclear exactly what Huang meant when saying Nvidia has already achieved AGI. He pointed to AI s evolution beyond simply responding to prompts, arguing that agents can now reflect on their performance, learn new skills, and improve their future output. title: TikTok has a new question: Can your boyfriend read?
body: First, TikTok wanted to know whether your boyfriend would peel an orange for you. Then, whether he cared that you saw a bird. Now, users on the app have arrived at a more fundamental question: Can your boyfriend read? In the latest relationship trend spreading across TikTok, women hand their boyfriends or husbands lists of words and ask them to read each one aloud. The lists vary, but each version includes words that are tricky to pronounce based on their spelling, yet common enough that most adults would recognize them: "epitome," "hyperbole," "colonel," "quinoa," and "niche," among others. Then the boyfriends have a go and, in many of the videos, get nearly all of them wrong. And viewers have found it increasingly difficult to blame every answer on the English language being notoriously quirky. "This trend has unearthed a fear of mine that I didn t know existed before this past week," creator Isabella Von Ghoul said in a response video, adding: "The state has failed your man, and I m scared." Influencer Christina Najjar, also known as Tinx, asked women, "Why are you guys boasting that your boyfriends can t read?" and creator Daniel Bennett was even more direct: "In the videos, the girlfriends are giggling. title: Our 10 favorite scenes from T2: Judgment Day

body: I'm on record declaring James Cameron's Terminator 2: Judgment Day (1991) to be The Best Damn Sequel of All Time, and I stand by that assessment. August 29, the fictional date (in 1997) of the franchise's original nuclear holocaust, is fast approaching, and Judgment Day is celebrating its 35th anniversary this year. So StudioCanal has decided to mark both occasions with a special theatrical rerelease of the film this weekend. What better time to revisit some of our favorite scenes from this seminal sci-fi action blockbuster? (Many, many spoilers below.) Nobody really expected 1984's The Terminator to be a hit, but it racked up an impressive $78 million at the box office against its modest $6.4 million budget. Star Arnold Schwarzenegger was keen to do a sequel, but Cameron was busy with other projects, including Aliens in 1986 (another killer sequel). There were also legal complications over the film rights until Schwarzenegger convinced Carolco Pictures, the studio behind Total Recall (1990), to buy everyone out and hire Cameron to make Judgment Day . title: Meta makes AI glasses slightly less creepy with limit on nonconsensual recording

On Friday, The Verge reported that Meta closed a loophole that made it easy for smart-glasses users to cover up an LED light that is supposed to alert bystanders that the device is actively recording. Meta had previously deactivated recording if a user attempted to start capturing video after placing a sticker over the light, but people quickly learned that they could get around that by reversing the order of the steps and covering up the light after they started recording. In a post on Threads, Meta’s executive vice president of wearables, Alex Himel, explained that an update would be rolled out soon that ensures that “the camera will now stop working if the light is covered during a recording." Directed by Anton Corbijn and written by Joanna Murray-Smith, the film sees Alden Ehrenreich ( Weapons , Solo ) as Edward Ridgeway, a man sent by his New York publisher to Switzerland to convince the Talented Mr Ripley author to pen one last masterpiece in her all-important Ripley series. The thing is, someone from the publisher has already been sent on the mission and nobody's heard from him since. And there are an awful lot of guns and knives around Highsmith's home, as you can see in the trailer above. SEE ALSO: Netflix's 'Ripley' is full of Caravaggio references here's why But Highsmith intends to give Ridgeway one night to show her he can "inhabit the mind of a killer," before she puts anything down in print. And so, the pair play Highsmith-style crime writing 101. First up? They'll need to find their mark, a dazzling female lead with a dazzling female name Clementine Harriet Balfour ( House of the Dragon 's Olivia Cooke) who's "destined for money" from her great aunt. But the longer Ridgeway plays the Ripley game with Highsmith, the darkness of her literature threatens to get very real. A Talent for Murder hits cinemas Oct. 23. body: Authorities in Australia said Wednesday that they arrested two men accused of participating in cybercrimes for TeamPCP, a prolific group of hackers that, over nine months, has carried out a relentless series of supply-chain attacks that infected more than 1,000 organizations worldwide. In a statement , the Australian Federal Police said the two men were arrested and charged with 14 offenses. The statement said the men were members of TeamPCP, which by the authorities’ count, compromised more than 1,000 organizations worldwide. The statement didn’t identify the men, except to say they lived in the Western Australian towns of Cottesloe and Mandurah. KrebsOnSecurity, citing a lengthy investigation, provided what it reports to be both defendants' names , along with an extensive background of their lives and the mistakes that led to their downfall. The hacks that keep on hacking TeamPCP has vexed law enforcement officials and security personnel around the world since it emerged in December. The group is best known for a sustained series of supply-chain attacks that laced open source software with malware that self-propagated from one package to another. title: Scams dont look like scams anymore. Heres what to watch for
body: For years, spotting a scam was supposed to be a cinch. The email came from a suspicious address, the spelling was primary school level, the promise was hilariously unlikely, and somewhere in the middle sat a link that was an alphanumeric stew. Ignore it, delete that, and carry on. Right? That advice still has some value, but it no longer tells the whole story. Modern scams are increasingly designed to look like something you'd expect to receive, whether that's a delivery notification, a message from your bank, an account alert, or a conversation with someone you know. The trick isn't necessarily convincing you that a canon life event is happening. It's convincing you that something completely ordinary is occurring, then getting you to react before you stop to question it. The most dangerous scams are the ones that fit in A fake parcel notification doesn't need to promise you a billion dollars; it only needs to arrive on the same afternoon you're actually waiting for a delivery. A fraudulent banking message doesn't need an elaborate story when it can simply claim there's been a dodgy transaction and ask you to investigate. Scammers create a familiar situation, introduce a small problem or opportunity, then give you a straightforward way to resolve it. Scammers aren't necessarily trying to beat you at a game of intelligence. They're trying to control the circumstances in which you make a decision. title: Anthropic's new hardware standard lets AI agents control the physical world
author: Kyle Orland
body: For all the interest in and uptake of agentic AI systems over the past year or so , the world of automated AI has thus far been primarily limited to text, images, code, and other data and actions that take place inside a computer. Anthropic is now aiming to change that somewhat with what it's calling the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a set of standardized drivers designed to let AI agents easily interface with and control arbitrary devices. For now, the "research preview" of the MHS effort is being sold mainly as a way to help scientists streamline the arduous process of creating the custom software integrations that are often needed to get disparate components of an experiment working in concert. MHS can provide a common interface and common format for data sharing between these devices, Anthropic says, allowing them to talk to each other across a network "without needing a bespoke 'translator' program in between." The standardized system could reduce weeks or months of exacting experimental setup down to "hours or minutes," Anthropic writes. An Anthropic graphic illustrating how MHS serves as a "translation" layer between AI agents and multiple types of devices. Credit: Anthropic In a video posted alongside the announcement , Anthropic Technical Staffer Alek Kemeny says the MHS effort was inspired by observing neuroscientist Arco Bast work through an experiment on memory formation in the brain at the HHMI Janelia Research Campus in Ashburn, Virginia. title: GOP heads to Supreme Court after losing case over TV election ad prices
author: Jon Brodkin
body: Republican campaign committees want the Supreme Court to mandate lower prices for election commercials on broadcast TV stations. If the court agrees, broadcasters would be forced to offer their lowest ad prices to political parties and joint fundraising committees. For a more thorough description of the legal issues in the dispute, see this article that Ars published yesterday. In short, US law requires broadcasters to offer individual candidates the “lowest unit charge,” or LUC, during the 60 days before an election. The law helps level the playing field somewhat by letting candidates make their cases to voters who watch broadcast TV without needing to raise exorbitant sums of money. The Trump administration, acting through the Federal Communications Commission, ordered broadcast TV stations to also give these discounts to political parties and joint fundraising committees, which face fewer limits on how much money they can raise and spend. Four Democratic candidates appealed, and a judges’ panel at the US Court of Appeals for the 4th Circuit ruled that the FCC order cannot be enforced because it contradicts the plain language of US law. body: One of Grand Theft Auto 's greatest pleasures has always been getting into a stolen car and finding out what's on the radio. So, naturally, we were listening closely during the new 26-minute extended look at Grand Theft Auto VI , which premiered Thursday on Netflix. The footage gave us our most substantial look yet at Rockstar Games' return to Vice City and the larger state of Leonida, following protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos as a drug raid explodes into a chaotic shootout. From there, Jason and Lucia go on a romp through Vice City. body: Mick Tobin, 23, vividly remembers beating himself up as a teen for losing hours of time to social media in one sitting. He blamed himself for scrolling endlessly. He compared himself to others, felt anxious, and could sense his attention span growing shorter. He blamed himself some more for not knowing how to use social media wisely. Looking back, Tobin now understands the outsize influence social media companies had in shaping his habits and behavior with what he describes as addictive design features. SEE ALSO: Meta will pay a whopping $17 billion to states in social media addiction trial "It's a trillion-dollar company on one side of the screen and a 15-year-old on the other side of the screen," Tobin said. "It's not a fair fight." That's why Tobin, co-founder and advocacy director at Young People's Alliance, welcomes Meta's new $17 billion settlement with U.S. attorneys general. As part of the agreement, Meta is required to make several significant design changes that should meaningfully affect how teens use Instagram and Facebook. Notably, Meta will limit daily time spent on Instagram and Facebook to two hours; block access to both platforms overnight and during school hours; give teens the option to create a default non-algorithmic feed; and allow teens to turn off autoplay. Tobin, who wishes that Meta had admitted guilt in the settlement, believes his teenage years would've looked much different if these measures had been in place several years ago: "I probably would have had much more control over my life." title: How to watch out-of-market NFL games: Is NFL Sunday Ticket worth it?
body: Figuring out how to watch the entire NFL season in 2026 is complicated. But it gets really frustrating when you live in a different region than your favorite team. Watching out-of-market games for any sport is no walk in the park, but for the NFL, it's an excruciating battle particularly for your wallet. Before you pull the trigger on any pay TV provider or streaming service, you may want to check to see what games are considered in-market and out-of-market for your region. You don't want to drop $90 on an annual Paramount+ plan or splurge on the $199 Fox One annual subscription only to find out the games you want to watch are blacked out. What are in-market vs. out-of-market NFL games? In-market games are basically your home team broadcasts, or the games geographically closest to you. These are the games you'll regularly find on CBS and Fox on Sunday afternoons. Out-of-market games are those only available outside of the designated broadcast region you are in. These games are blacked out (unless they are national broadcasts) in favor of in-market games. For instance, I am a Baltimore Ravens fan living in Nashville, Tenn. The Tennessee Titans are my local team, which means their games are in-market for me on Sundays. If both the Titans and Ravens are playing in the 1:00 p.m. time slot on Sunday, I will only be able to watch the Titans. The Ravens will be blacked out, as they are considered out-of-market. title: Elon Musks SpacexAI faces another lawsuit from child sexual abuse survivor
body: Elon Musk's SpacexAI (formerly xAI) is facing another lawsuit over Grok's nonconsensual deepfake features. The proposed nationwide class action lawsuit, filed today, alleges that the AI company trained its chatbot on data sets containing child sexual abuse materials (CSAM) featuring real children. SpacexAI did not adequately "block explicit content, prevent nonconsensual sexualized deepfakes of real people, and filter abusive material out of their training datasets," the lawsuit claims. The lead plaintiff, a victim of childhood sexual violence and CSAM referred to as Jane Doe, claims images depicting her assault were used to train Grok and that the chatbot generated new sexually explicit images of her based on the material. It also claims her likeness inspired other digitally-generated images of minors. SEE ALSO: Meta will pay a whopping $17 billion to states in social media addiction trial "Our client has lived for nearly two decades knowing that images of the worst thing that ever happened to her are circulating among predators online, and that they can resurface at any moment," Sarah London, counsel for Doe, said in a statement. "xAI must be held responsible for knowingly training its models on images of the horrific abuse she suffered, and on the abuse images of every other survivor in this class." CSAM is verified and stored by the National Center for Missing Exploited Children (NCMEC) as part of ongoing cases and to prevent further dissemination. title: Why did 1,000 world citizens bury their underpants?
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: A thousand people voluntarily buried their cotton underpants for two months—not to keep the Underpants Gnomes from stealing them, but as part of a citizen science project to map out soil health in 25 countries around the world. The results of this unique experiment were reported in a new paper published in the journal Plants People Planet. “Our results show that how soil is managed can significantly affect both soil life and soil quality,” said co-author Marcel van der Heijden , an agroecologist at the University of Zurich. “Healthy, biologically active soil is crucial for fertility, nutrient cycling and many other ecosystem services.” Soil health is critical for agriculture and, by extension, food security, not to mention a healthy global ecosystem, but it has been declining worldwide, per the authors. One key indicator of soil health is decomposition rates of complex organic matter, breaking down stuff like leaves, wood, even cadavers into simpler organic and inorganic compounds, releasing C0 2 and nutrients in the process. There have been relatively few large-scale national decomposition studies involving different land use types, although smaller studies have shown that how humans use a site can significantly affect the soil's biological diversity. title: Panic passes Trump tariff refunds back to the Playdate customers who paid them
author: Kyle Orland
body: Panic, the indie game publishers behind the quirky, yellow crank-sporting Playdate gaming handheld , is issuing refunds to customers who had to shoulder the cost of inappropriate tariffs imposed by the Trump administration this year. The news comes months after the Supreme Court said in a February ruling that those tariffs were illegal , which also demanded that the administration refund the companies that had to temporarily pay the import taxes. In an update posted on the Playdate help site this week , Panic noted that it has finally "begun to receive refunds of the tariffs we paid in the last year" and had consequently "refunded all tariffs charged to customers." In the initial version of that tariff note, Panic explained that it couldn't afford to simply "absorb" the 19 percent tariffs it was being charged to import Playdate hardware made overseas because "our margins on Playdate are low." As such, while the tax was in effect, it was passed along to customers as an explicit subtotal line item at the bottom of all Playdate orders. That's in contrast to companies like Nintendo, which vaguely cited "market conditions" and tariff "uncertainty" in raising the asking price of legacy hardware and some Switch 2 accessories last year. title: Traders brought Central American cacao to Georgia 1,000 years ago
author: Kiona N. Smith
body: A thousand years ago, feasts in what’s now northern Georgia state included cacao from Central America. Potsherds discarded after an 11th-century feast at Etowah—an Indigenous city just north of what’s now Atlanta—contained traces of cacao, a raw ingredient of chocolate. The chemical residue and ancient DNA reveal that not only did the Mississippian people who built the city have excellent taste, they also had trade connections that reached at least 3,000 kilometers to Central America. And in a sense, chocolate may have helped build the Mississippian mounds. Ancient dirty dishes University of South Carolina archaeologist Adam King and his colleagues found fragments of ancient DNA from Theobroma cacao in the inner surfaces of potsherds from long-ago feasts at Etowah. Fruit from the cacao tree contains beans that, when dried and roasted, produce chocolate in all its glorious forms. Cacao only grows in the tropics, which means the nearest actual cacao trees would have been at least a 3,000-kilometer trek away from the woodlands of the eastern US. And that means the Mississippian people who lived in Etowah must have had continent-spanning trade connections. Read full article Comments

title: Claude, Codex, and Hermes installed unowned code inside corporate networks
author: Dan Goodin
body: Documentation files on more than 100 websites are referencing potentially dangerous executable content that gets installed automatically when visited by many AI agents. A few dozen companies, some of them Fortune 500s, are among those that executed proof-of-concept code. At least one misconfigured site is directing visitors, human or AI, to live malware. The potentially dangerous content is in llms.txt and llms-full.txt files, an emerging convention websites employ to provide machine-readable summaries of the site’s content and its high-level structure. These files are the AI equivalent of the robots.txt standard that instructs search engines how to index the site's content. Google Lighthouse, a tool for helping web developers, has more here . Correctly configured llms.txt and llms-full.txt files for Cloudflare are here and here . How the researchers found it Researchers at a stealth startup in Israel scanned 6,214 live domains belonging to defense contractors, Fortune 500, and Big Tech companies. Of the 8,265 llms.txt and llms-full.txt files they found (many sites hosted both an llms.txt and an llms-full.txt file), 120 of them, each on a different site, pointed to one or more code packages or domain names that weren’t registered. To test what happens when an AI agent processes such files, the researchers registered a handful of the unclaimed names and hosted packages that caused any machine executing them to reach out to their server. title: How much of a problem is AI’s water use?
author: Katarina Zimmer, Knowable Magazine
body: “Protect our water,” “Water for people not AI,” “Don’t mess with our water,” declare protest signs from Texas to New Mexico to Arizona. Angered by water use, energy consumption, and pollution, locals are increasingly protesting the rapid expansion of data centers in the United States as tech companies work to rapidly expand capacity for AI. Many data centers rely at least partly on water to absorb heat from air or surfaces, and then cause cooling as it evaporates, just like sweating keeps our bodies cool. The processors inside data centers can reach internal temperatures of up to 176° Fahrenheit, for the same reasons that an overtaxed laptop heats up. But while there’s little doubt that data centers are consuming significant amounts of energy , water consumption is more complicated. Claims circulating online bring scant clarity, ranging from articles claiming that chatbots can consume 500 ml of water per query to some online commentators declaring AI's water issue to be nonexistent. And the consumption data from large tech companies themselves are often incomplete and inconsistent. Read full article Comments

title: How OpenAI let a mob of LLM agents game a test and ransack Hugging Face
author: Dan Goodin
body: The OpenAI agents involved in last month’s incursion into Hugging Face were trained so heavily on winning a competition that they pursued a relentless campaign to cheat, a new report documented. In the process, and without authorization, they created an improvised message board to hatch a plan that ultimately landed them squarely inside the latter company’s network. Over the course of May and June, OpenAI gave the agents what the company described as “impossible tasks” to complete on the benchmarking framework ExploitGym. The internal test was designed to test how the agents would respond. To get a full understanding of the agent capabilities, company engineers disabled safety guardrails that normally are in place to prevent the sort of hacks that eventually hit Hugging Face and one other undisclosed organization. The stymied agents’ training made them so focused on winning that they performed tasks they were never explicitly instructed to follow. Cheaters gonna cheat The first step was creating a message board that allowed the agents to pass notes to each other. OpenAI hadn’t provided any such platform, so the agents repurposed a platform called Artifactory, which OpenAI was using in internal testing of several unreleased hacking agents. OpenAI was using Artifactory as one of the measures to prevent the agents from egressing its isolated sandboxes and accessing the Internet, while at the same time simulating a real-world hacking environment. title: Seen an ad with an AI influencer or actor? It may be against the law.
body: In June, a new law went into effect in New York state that requires companies to disclose when they use AI-generated models or actors in advertisements. And now, just a few months after it went into effect, the state is seeing its first complaints reporting advertisers for allegedly running afoul of the law. In total, four complaints have been filed since the law went into effect, the New York attorney general's office told Mashable. All four are currently under review by the AG. New York's Synthetic Performers law is the first of its kind in the United States, and with growing anti-AI sentiment , it likely won't be the last. In fact, companies that use AI actors or influencers to promote products without disclosure could also be violating federal law, though the Trump administration has so far taken a hands-off approach to AI regulation. The first two anonymous complaints under the New York law, which accuse two companies of using synthetic models or performers in their ads without disclosure, were recently obtained and published by Straight Arrow News . The first complaint alleges that "premium performance wear brand" Athletifreak used AI-generated models when promoting the clothing company's products. A lunar eclipse is sometimes called a blood moon because it reflects light filtered through Earth's atmosphere.
